blocks.x: Quantum Machine Learning & Simulation sits in the Quantum & Advanced Compute tower, and it earns that place by being specific: QML and simulation pilots with industrial honesty — real baselines, real data, real verdicts. The build pattern, the artifacts and the guardrails follow.

Quantum machine learning and quantum simulation sit on the research frontier, and enterprises deserve honest engagement with it. We run structured pilots: kernel-method classification on carefully chosen feature subsets, variational approaches where problem structure suggests advantage, and simulation workloads (materials, chemistry, fluid dynamics adjacent) benchmarked against the best classical methods — DFT, molecular dynamics, HPC baselines — on identical data and evaluation protocols.

Every pilot ends in one of three documented verdicts: advantage demonstrated (rare, valuable — proceed to industrialization), parity reached (monitor as hardware improves), no advantage at current scale (file the negative result and revisit triggers). This discipline protects your credibility while building genuine internal capability in quantum algorithms and their honest evaluation.

Quantum Machine Learning & Simulation delivery today concentrates in Healthcare & Life Sciences, Energy & Utilities, Manufacturing & Industrial, Banking & Financial Services. The metric is chosen with your finance lead, and the baseline is signed before any build begins.
What ships, in the order it ships:

items: Pilot design
problem selection with classical baselines and evaluation protocol pre-agreed
QML experimentation
kernel methods and variational approaches on curated enterprise data
Simulation benchmarking
quantum vs. classical (DFT/MD/HPC) on identical protocols
Verdict discipline
advantage / parity / no-advantage outcomes with documented evidence
Revisit triggers
hardware and algorithm milestones that reopen closed cases
